headline: China is rapidly building AI data centres in its energy-rich inland regions, with 89 built or planned in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, alone.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: a major financial paper's report on China's AI infrastructure build-out; text read on a relay, original blocked.
importance_line: It matters for power supply in China's inland regions and for the race with the US over AI computing, but the report describes data centres that are built or planned, so how much of this capacity will run is not yet known.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by BigGo Finance, that China is significantly expanding data centre construction in inland regions rich in energy, with 89 data centres built or planned in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, alone. BigGo Finance adds that China is trying to narrow its gap with the US in AI while struggling to obtain advanced AI chips.
